_about: Liberty Lights prototype sounds. The four fireworks are the gameplay cues and must never be confused: boom is all low end (a mortar thump and a rolling bass burst), crackle is a high scatter of tiny pops with almost no body, whistle is a rising pitched shriek ending in a small pop, sparkle is a soft glassy shimmer with a hiss. Fireworks, the launch and the aim tick are mono on purpose: the game places them left, centre or right with play_at. Crowd reactions get louder and brighter as accuracy rises: cheer (80 percent and up), ooh (60 and up), aah (40 and up), a confused murmur below that. Music is a fife-and-drum Yankee Doodle loop for the title, kept quiet under speech, plus pass, fail and finale stingers.

sounds._arrangement: 64 beats: A; A2 with a second fife a third below; B, a new fife strain over C and A minor; a fife-and-snare breakdown with the bass drum back in its last bar.

sounds._about: Menu select: a small pop with a sparkle.
Menu back: a soft distant thump.
Pause music: a fife tune slowed down over strings, the crowd waiting.

_score: The fairground band's score: tuba and horns always, alone while a show plays so the fireworks stand clear; the drums, the fife tune and its harmony join as you launch your own show and as the levels climb; snare rolls and glockenspiel through the grand finale. The danger stem is not used.
